en: Taal Volcano is unique because its main crater is an island located inside a lake that is also inside a larger volcano.
The Puerto Princesa Subterranean River in Palawan is one of the few rivers in the world that flows directly from a mountain straight into the ocean.
Mount Pulag, the highest peak in Luzon, is famous for its magical sea of clouds phenomenon where thick clouds sit below the mountain peak.
Lake Danao in Leyte is uniquely shaped exactly like a guitar and is surprisingly located high up on top of a mountain.
The Verde Island Passage in Batangas is scientifically recognized as the center of marine shorefish biodiversity, containing more fish species than any other place on Earth.
The Philippines experiences a unique dual monsoon climate where the Amihan brings cool northeast winds, while the Habagat brings heavy southwest rains.
The Philippines holds some of the world's largest reserves of nickel, making it a top global exporter of this crucial metal used for batteries.
The famous Chocolate Hills in Bohol consist of over 1,200 perfectly cone-shaped mounds that turn brown during the dry season, resembling giant chocolate kisses.
The long, narrow province of Palawan acts as a massive geographical barrier that physically separates the South China Sea from the Sulu Sea.
The Philippine tarsier, a tiny primate found in Bohol, has eyes that are actually larger than its brain to help it see in dark forests.
The Tubbataha Reefs Natural Park in the Sulu Sea is a protected UNESCO site that is only accessible to divers for three months a year.
The small island province of Camiguin has seven volcanoes, meaning it has a higher number of volcanoes than it has individual municipalities.
